# TEST-GAP-07: the RPC method coverage ratchet, read by
# `rpc_every_method_has_success_and_refusal_test` in `src/rpc/method_class.rs`.
#
# One line per gap: `<method> missing=success` or `<method> missing=refusal`.
# A row of `METHOD_CLASSES` is covered when a test function in `src/rpc/tests.rs`
# or `src/tests/*.rs` names the method (its JSON-RPC name in quotes, or a call to
# its handler) and the statement that names it unwraps an answer (success) or
# reads the error (refusal).
#
# Two kinds of row carry a smaller demand, and the rule encodes both, so a line
# here is always work a later change can finish:
#   * a `Refused` row is not asked for a success test, because it refuses every
#     call by design and its refusal must name the transaction door;
#   * a method `src/rpc/api.rs` declares with the receiver alone is not asked for
#     a refusal test, because it has no invalid call at that layer and an error
#     case for it would be an invention.
#
# The file only shrinks. A line whose test exists must be deleted in the same
# change, and a method that loses its test must be recorded here with a reason in
# the pull request that does it. The gate's own behaviour is locked by
# `rpc_method_coverage_catches_an_injected_gap`.
#
# Measured against the tree on 2026-11-06: 183 rows, 48 rows covered
# on both sides the rule asks for, 135 rows carrying 204 gap lines.
